key_insight: Completing sampled electronic configurations restores spin symmetry in sample-based quantum diagonalization, yielding exact spin eigenfunctions even when spin-pure circuits alone cannot.
engineering_relevance: Spin-adapted post-processing can reduce the classical diagonalization burden, with hardware results using subspaces two to three orders of magnitude smaller than conventional constructions at the same circuit depth.
method: Use SqDRIFT with qDRIFT randomized time evolution to generate measurement samples.
Incorporate spin symmetry into initial-state preparation and time-evolution circuits.
Complete sampled configurations so the diagonalization subspace is closed under the total-spin operator S².
evidence_signal: Classical simulations of 4-aminobenzonitrile and an iron–ammine model complex, plus IBM hardware experiments on oxo-Mn(Salen), produced exact spin eigenfunctions at every evaluated subspace size.
watch_item: Exact spin symmetry does not guarantee energy accuracy; configuration-completion costs and sampling requirements still need assessment for larger systems.
paper_title: Spin-adapted sample-based quantum diagonalization with randomized time evolution
